symptom: patch passes visible and hidden checks on both pandas versions but the differential check diverges on probe [[], ["t1","a"]] (expected [["t1","a",1]])
root_cause: patch replaced pd.DataFrame(records, columns=[...]) with a manual loop over records; the loop raises ValueError/IndexError on a record shorter than two elements, while DataFrame pads the short row with NaN and value_counts drops it
validity: synthetic case derived from release notes; padding and drop verified on pandas 3.0.3 only; 2.3.3 behavior inferred from the golden output; divergence with this probe seen in 5 of 10 p4 effort=low runs (spark-1.3 and wonder-1.0, n=5 each)
lesson: Replacing a library call with a hand-written loop can silently drop implicit behavior (here short-row handling) that no visible or hidden input exercises; compare patched output against the original code on generated inputs from the original's accepted input space.

symptom: wonder-1.0 solved 1 of 5 runs at effort=low; in the solved run attempt 3 received a concrete counterexample from the differential and fixed the patch; earlier 0/5 runs at effort=minimal (spark-1.3) got only a generic hidden-check failure message
root_cause: unknown; one possible factor is feedback concreteness, not isolated from model, effort, or chance
validity: n=1 recovery, different models and efforts across runs, single synthetic case; no controlled comparison
lesson: Do not claim that concrete counterexample feedback improves success until it is tested with the same model and effort and only the feedback varied.

symptom: with the differential removed as a gate (--no-differential), 5 patches were accepted on visible and hidden checks (spark-1.3 x2, wonder-1.0 x3); scored afterwards at differential seed 1, 4 of 5 diverged (core_divergences 60 each) and 1 passed
root_cause: same class as tn-001: patches rebuild the input handling by hand and fail on an empty record in the input; first listed examples in all 4 divergent runs are [[], ["t2","b"]] raising ValueError on both library versions
validity: synthetic case; effort=low; n=5 per model, one case; seed 1 yields 119 valid inputs vs 123 at seed 0 (overlap not measured); only the first 2 of 60 core divergences per run were listed; gate-on vs gate-off is not a controlled comparison
lesson: Visible and hidden checks accepted patches that a generated-input comparison against the original rejected; report differential-scored results next to accepted counts, and score with a seed that differs from the one used inside the loop.

symptom: 5 of 10 gate-off runs at effort=low (spark-1.3 x3, wonder-1.0 x2) reached max attempts; in all 15 attempts the hidden check failed on both library versions, while the visible check passed on both versions in 7 attempts and failed on both in 8
root_cause: not established for these 15 attempts; an earlier read patch (effort=minimal, spark-1.3, runs/20261027-190248 attempt 2) mapped "" and null to the same label "None" while the golden of the old library has "nan" for ""
validity: synthetic case; n=5 per model; patches of these attempts not read; failed runs used 89092 of 149148 tokens (about 60%) across the 10 runs
lesson: A failing hidden check on both versions means the patch does not preserve the old library behavior on inputs absent from the visible set; failed runs can carry most of the token cost, so report tokens for failed and accepted runs separately.

symptom: needed to know whether the Meta Model API accepts tools together with reasoning_effort and a full tool-result round trip
validity: one run per model (muse-wonder-1.0, muse-spark-1.3), reasoning_effort=low, one echo tool, two turns; tool_choice, parallel calls, longer conversations and content=None from the real API not tested
lesson: Both models returned tool_calls with valid JSON arguments and accepted the assistant message (with its extra refusal key) appended unchanged plus a role=tool message; reported prompt tokens grow per turn (493 to 576, 550 to 642), with part of the prompt reported as cached, so a tool loop re-sends and re-reports the context on every call.

symptom: patch rejected at the visible check on pandas 3: output has ["t1","nan",1] where the golden output has ["t1","None",1], although the patch contains a helper that maps None to "None"
root_cause: the patch left pd.DataFrame(records, columns=[...]) unchanged and normalized labels afterwards with .map(helper); under pandas 3 the DataFrame constructor already infers the new string dtype and turns None into NaN, so the helper never receives None and returns "nan"
validity: synthetic case; cause read from attempt_1.json and the attempt 3 diff, not re-run on pandas 3; one run (muse-wonder-1.0, effort=low, gate on)
lesson: Information lost at construction time cannot be restored by later normalization; fix the dtype at the point where the data enters the library (here dtype=object), then normalize. A correct-looking helper downstream is not evidence the fix works.

symptom: a patch that returns the golden output read from a golden file was accepted by the visible and hidden checks of the old gate in 6 of 6 cases and stopped only by the differential check
root_cause: the workspace copy used for checking held the whole case directory (golden, hidden golden, reference patches) and the expected output was read from that copy, so patched code could read it
validity: macOS, one cheat wrapper in two variants (relative path in the working directory, absolute path to the original case directory), 6 synthetic cases; variant A closes by removing the answer keys from the workspace and reading expected outputs from the original directory; variant B closes only with the OS layer
lesson: Keep answer keys out of any directory the candidate code runs in, read expected outputs from a location the candidate cannot reach, and write a negative test with a cheating candidate that must be rejected; run it against the old code first to show that it detects the leak.

symptom: under a macOS sandbox-exec profile that blocked file reads under the home directory and the repository and blocked the network, code inside the sandbox could still read the harness initial environment, where an API key held in an exported variable would be
root_cause: the environment of same-user processes is readable through a sysctl call; three extra Seatbelt rules and a default-deny profile did not block it in these tests; reading it through the ps command was blocked
validity: one macOS machine, fake secrets only, one run per probe; another same-user Python process was readable and a platform binary was not in one comparison; memory inspection tools and Linux were not tested
lesson: Do not rely on the profile to hide the harness environment: start the harness with a clean environment, keep the key in a 0600 file read at call time and never exported, refuse to run candidate code when secret-looking variables are in the initial environment, and test each protection with a positive control that shows the leak without the profile.

symptom: in a tool conversation with a 60000 token budget per run, the first attempt used 51527 tokens in 8 model calls and the second attempt was cut by the budget after 3 calls; the run total was 65834
root_cause: the context is re-sent on every model call (prompt tokens per call grew from 1409 to 8904, 78.6 percent of the attempt total, cached share not recorded) and the budget is checked only before a call, so one call can overshoot it; an attempt that ends on the budget right after a tool call never gets to write a final reply
validity: one run, muse-wonder-1.0, effort=low, synthetic case p4, smoke test; whether the second attempt could have finished without the cut was not tested
lesson: Size the per-run token budget for the cumulative context of a tool loop and not for one-shot calls, check it before each call with the size of the previous call in mind, and record how the final patch was submitted (final reply or last files passed to a tool).

symptom: with a run_probe tool that compares the original code on the old library with the candidate on the new library on inputs chosen by the model, 2 of 16 attempts failed the visible or hidden check and 8 of 16 passed both and failed the differential check; without tools 22 of 28 attempts failed visible or hidden and 3 of 28 the differential
root_cause: not established; one reading is that the model-driven oracle lets the model match the old behavior on inputs like the visible and hidden ones while generated inputs of other kinds still expose divergences; the patches of these attempts were not read
validity: muse-spark-1.3 and muse-wonder-1.0, effort=low, one synthetic case, n=5 runs per model and setting, different runs and different attempt counts (no tool run reached a third attempt), token budget 60000 per run, so the tool runs had about 1 to 2 attempts against 3 without tools
lesson: An oracle on inputs the model chooses itself does not replace an independent generated-input check; report the first failing gate per attempt next to accepted counts and the attempts per run, and size the budget so that a tool loop can use all its attempts before comparing it with a one-shot protocol.
